clue.text: Inform on one held by senior of luminaries

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase meaning belonging to the stars

indicators.note: being held by something means sitting inside it, so the senior abbreviation wraps the rest

parts.note: to inform on someone is to tell on them
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A grass reports on one of the leading lights to a senior figure among the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Luminaries are stars, and the adjective for things to do with stars is this one.

clue.text: Reason? It takes that to get into US city

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is also called 'it'

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so the pronoun goes inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York
the pronoun 'that' can be replaced by it

explanation.surface: A remark that only a sound mind lets you into an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is sex appeal, SA, a crossword staple; 'that' gives IT, which goes inside NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of a sound mind, as in losing one's reason.

clue.text: Cook pie, that's what to do with ham for food lover

indicators.note: to cook something can mean to doctor it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ham is cured, preserved with salt or smoke

explanation.surface: Instructions for baking a pie and curing ham, offered to a gourmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges PIE into EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a gourmet, a person of refined taste in eating.

clue.text: They've a role at sea and sentence lads soundly

indicators.note: soundly says the words are to be heard aloud rather than read

parts.note: a life sentence and boys for lads

explanation.surface: Lads handed a long prison sentence get a part to play on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'role' plays on roll: the rings bob on the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating rings are thrown to people in the water to keep them afloat.

clue.text: Those turning to take off what makes one fleet of foot

definitions.text: what makes one fleet of foot

parts.note: rollers are things that turn over and over

indicators.note: off means awry or not right, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Things that spin, ready for take-off, make someone quick on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TAKE into KATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot on wheels lets the wearer glide along fast.

clue.text: Try a race to secure office worker

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so the race letters go round the worker

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
a temp is a temporary office worker

explanation.surface: Someone attempts a race in order to land a temp for the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT, the Isle of Man motorcycle race, is a crossword staple; 'to secure' is the container signal, so the race wraps the temp.
explanation.definitionFit: To try something is to make an effort or bid at it.

clue.text: A ship's passengers will in-elude a silly person

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the answer is found inside the word

explanation.surface: Among those aboard ship there is bound to be a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey stands for foolishness, so the word names a fool.

clue.text: Went underground coming up for first appearance

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a debut is a first appearance

explanation.surface: Someone surfaces from below for their opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: To tube is to travel by the London Underground, known as the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelled on the London Tube, the city's underground railway network.

clue.text: French husband holds can of drink

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the husband word goes round the can

parts.note: mari is French for husband
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's husband grips a can of something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Cheap time by women to start on the Big Apple

parts.note: to open is to start
the Big Apple is New York, NY

explanation.surface: A cheap time for women to begin on New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is only a link here. Two-penny goods cost two old British pence, hence trifling or cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Costing two old pence, so worth very little: a word for something trifling.

clue.text: Dossiers at one's finger tips?

parts.note: dossiers are files, and files used at the tips of the fingers are the ones for shaping the nails

explanation.surface: Records kept handy, ready to consult at a moment's notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At one's fingertips' normally means close to hand, but here it is literal: the tool filed at the ends of the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Small abrasive tools for shaping fingernails, read as a pun on files meaning dossiers.

clue.text: Brother tethers ancient city donkey

indicators.note: tethering ties something in place, so the brother word holds the city inside it

parts.note: Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A monk ties up a donkey belonging to an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: A burro is a small donkey used as a pack animal, a word from Spanish.

clue.text: Try to get lift in ancient Humber

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words, running across their join

explanation.surface: A hitchhiker tries to get a ride in an old Humber car.
explanation.walkthrough: A Humber was a British make of car, which makes 'lift' sound like a ride in one.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb is to hitchhike, signalling drivers with a raised digit for a ride.

clue.text: Drug record by man had, in short, upset Erin

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
HE, the male pronoun, stands for a man
had is shortened to 'd, as in I'd

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and rearranged, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone who took a record-related drug has disturbed a girl called Erin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges ERIN to RINE, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephedrine is a stimulant drug used as a decongestant and once in asthma treatment.

clue.text: Rodents as one might gather?

parts.note: to gather crops is to harvest, so small rodents one might gather are named after that word

explanation.surface: Rodents, as you might have guessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As one might gather' sounds like 'as you might suppose', but gather here means to reap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny rodents that nest among cereal stalks take their name from reaping time.

clue.text: Corn set to be ruined, row

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Corn set to be ruined, row' (14), gives anagram of CORN SET plus RUCTION for row, but no word is left to define RECONSTRUCTION; clue seems cut short and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Corn set to be ruined, row

clue.text: Dye company feature brewing of ale

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: brewing stirs things up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A dye business makes a point of its ale brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing of' rearranges ALE into EAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a red dye made from crushed insects, used as food colouring.

clue.text: Forgotten state of outside broadcast with violin playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A broadcast from outdoors features a violin being played, then forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges VIOLIN into LIVION.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition of being forgotten, or of being unaware, as in falling into obscurity.

clue.text: In case a hobble's used on crossing these might help?

indicators.note: the letters are put to use in a new order, signalling a rearrangement of the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone hobbling across the road might be helped by these crossing lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges all of IN CASE A HOBBLES. BELISHA BEACONS are the flashing amber globes on poles that mark British zebra crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashing amber lamps mark pedestrian crossings in Britain, helping walkers cross safely.

clue.text: Good friend about to secure victory for flier

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly inside, so the turned letters go round the victory word
about signals a turnaround, so the good and friend letters are read backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A good mate is about to clinch a win for the pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns both the good and friend letters, giving LAPG; 'to secure' then holds the victory word inside, before the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapwing is a crested plover, a bird and so a creature of flight.

clue.text: Bid makes one anything but bottom

parts.note: anything but means not at all
the rump is the bottom

explanation.surface: An attempt that makes someone anything but the lowest.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a bid to play without a trump suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a contract bid with no trump suit named.

clue.text: British comfort, we hear, of gentle zephyr

indicators.note: the clue speaks of what is heard, so the letters are judged by sound

parts.note: BR is British, and comfort is ease

explanation.surface: The British idea of comfort is a soft westerly wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A zephyr is a light wind, a mild current of air.

clue.text: Job wasn't so demanding?

parts.note: Job of the Bible is proverbial for patience; demanding things at once is the opposite trait

explanation.surface: A complaint that a piece of work was less taxing than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' at the start of the clue hides the capital: it is the biblical Job, famous for his patience, not a task.
explanation.definitionFit: Being restless and wanting things now is the reverse of the patience of Job.

clue.text: Touch high tension and you could be stiff

parts.note: tig is the children's chasing game also called tag, played by touching
T is used as an abbreviation for tension

explanation.surface: Touching a high-tension cable could leave you rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: Stiff and tight both mean drunk, as well as rigid. TIG is the British name for the playground game of tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for being drunk, as well as meaning rigid or taut.

clue.text: Fashionable territory to provide ground cover?

parts.note: IN means fashionable or trendy
Ter. is an abbreviation for territory

explanation.surface: A gardener plans to plant trendy ground cover across a patch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground cover' suggests plants, but it means covering with earth, as in a burial.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body is to give it a covering of earth.

clue.text: Taking a chance with day off to get cake decoration

indicators.note: off means removed, so the letter for day is taken away

parts.note: dicing, as in dicing with death, is taking risks

explanation.surface: A gambler takes a day off to get a decoration for a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar frosting spread over a cake is its decorative top coat.

clue.text: How to get lure of old calculating device?

parts.note: slide the letters of rule along and they spell lure

explanation.surface: Advice on catching something with a bait from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: slide the R of RULE to the end and it becomes LURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Before electronic calculators, engineers multiplied with a ruler-like instrument of sliding logarithmic scales.

clue.text: In brief, is certainly to speak

parts.note: is in brief is the contraction 's
ay is an old form of aye, yes

explanation.surface: A short way of saying that something is surely to be spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something is to speak it.

clue.text: Theatre performances could be in the manner of a Sir, we hear

indicators.note: the clue speaks of what is heard, so the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.words: in the manner of a Sir
parts.note: a Sir is a knight, so behaving like one is knightly

explanation.surface: Stage shows might be put on with the grand airs of a theatrical knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Shows given every evening are said to run each night.

clue.text: See failing to limit cut as unenlightenment?

indicators.note: limiting something means bounding it on each side, so the shuffled letters enclose the cut
failing means breaking down, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: to clip is to cut

explanation.surface: Not being able to see is described as unenlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges the word see into ESE; 'to limit' has those letters bound the cut on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon blocks the sun, the light goes out: a literal loss of illumination.
